candidates.question: An administrator configures an Active branch ruleset for main in a public repository. The agent has no bypass permission. 'Require branches to be up to date before merging' is selected, but no required check has been defined. What configuration omission explains why selecting that option alone provides no up-to-date protection?

answerChoices.text: The ruleset must be moved from Active to Disabled while the agent opens its PR.
A commit-message metadata restriction must be added to the existing ruleset.
The agent must receive a For pull requests only bypass entry.
An actual required status check must be defined in the ruleset.

candidates.explanation: The up-to-date requirement takes effect only when a required check is defined. Define the intended check as a requirement in the ruleset.
candidates.deepExplanation: Enforcement status, branch targeting, and bypass are already constrained in the scenario. The source specifically qualifies the up-to-date option with a required-check dependency; naming a convention or adding metadata restrictions cannot supply that dependency.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: Disabling the rule removes enforcement rather than supplying the missing required check.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.b: Metadata restrictions do not define the status check required for the up-to-date setting to take effect.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: Giving bypass permission does not establish the omitted validation dependency and would relax the agent's restrictions.

candidates.question: A team removes the explicit GITHUB_TOKEN input from an action used by an agent workflow and concludes that the action can no longer use that token. The workflow still grants write permissions. What documented property invalidates that conclusion?

answerChoices.text: A GitHub App installation token can supply permissions unavailable to GITHUB_TOKEN.
A PAT stored as a repository secret can be referenced explicitly in a workflow.
An action can access github.token even without an explicit GITHUB_TOKEN input.

candidates.explanation: Actions can access github.token without an explicit token input. Control the granted permissions instead.
candidates.deepExplanation: Token delivery and token authority are different. The documentation recommends least-required permissions rather than relying on omission of a parameter.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.A: The stated action already has a GITHUB_TOKEN access path; no App token is needed to explain it. Alternate context: Use an installation token when the workflow requires permissions GITHUB_TOKEN cannot provide.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.B: No PAT is involved in the stated conclusion about implicit GITHUB_TOKEN access. Alternate context: A secret-stored PAT fits a separately authorized workflow credential requirement.

candidates.question: A Copilot cloud agent task accesses a service through three paths: an agent Bash-started command inside the Actions appliance, an MCP server, and a configured setup step. The security design proposes using only the agent firewall to constrain all three paths. Which assessment follows the documented coverage boundary?

answerChoices.text: The firewall covers the Bash-started appliance process; the MCP and setup-step paths need separate controls.

candidates.question: An organization custom firewall rule permits an entire package domain for Copilot cloud agent. A repository administrator adds a narrower URL rule but the organization grant remains. Repository custom rules are allowed, and the recommended list has no overlapping grant. Which change addresses the broad organization access?

answerChoices.text: Disable the recommended allowlist.
Ask the organization owner to enable repository-added custom rules.
Have an organization owner narrow or remove the organization custom entry.

candidates.explanation: The allowlists combine. The repository's narrower addition does not subtract the organization rule.
candidates.deepExplanation: This is a rule-composition issue, not a claim that every repository setting is editable. Organization locks on other firewall settings still apply.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.A: The broad grant is explicitly an organization custom entry with no overlapping recommended entry. Alternate context: Changing the recommended list fits a decision to remove its default dependency-host grants, subject to organization policy.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.B: That setting is already enabled and does not remove an organization entry. Alternate context: Enable repository custom rules when administrators need to add entries and organization policy currently forbids them.

candidates.question: A repository evaluation job runs an agent's proposed changes and produces a coverage report plus detailed failure files. Reviewers need those files after the workflow finishes, not just a pass/fail status. Which documented mechanism preserves the generated evidence for inspection?

answerChoices.text: Download a previously uploaded artifact without uploading the newly generated files.
Upload the generated reports and failure files as workflow artifacts.
Set a retention-days value without including the files in an artifact upload.

candidates.explanation: Upload the actual generated evidence files as named workflow artifacts.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: Downloading an existing artifact does not preserve the new report and failure files.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: Retention configures how long an uploaded artifact is stored; it does not select and upload the evidence by itself.
